atlas-om.0046: In the Ministry of Higher Education’s Employer Survey 2025, employers favoured graduates in management, commerce, engineering and information technology, especially bachelor’s holders. We found no page where Omani employers rank foreign universities; a foreign degree needs Ministry of Higher Education equivalency.
atlas-om.0047: Sultan Qaboos University Career Fair: 13–15 April 2026, with Oman Arab Bank among the exhibitors and the Ministry of Labour’s under-secretary at the opening.
atlas-om.0048: Oman Internship Fair 2026: 26 January 2026, 9:00 to 14:00 at The Diplomatic Club in Muscat, more than 65 companies, for students and fresh graduates.
atlas-om.0049: Sohar University Career Training Fair: 2–4 February 2026, an exhibition with public and private bodies and workshops on labour-market skills.
atlas-om.0050: The central bank’s 2013 circular tells banks to strive for Omanisation above 90% overall, with 100% for clerical staff and senior-management targets of 75% and 90%; foreign banks may exempt their CEO or country manager and a single-branch foreign bank may have three non-Omani staff.
atlas-om.0051: Accounting is one of the regulated professions for which expatriates must have their qualifications assessed and approved by accredited sectoral skills units before arrival; KPMG Middle East’s two-year Audit track assesses English, logical and numerical reasoning and accounting online.
atlas-om.0052: PDO’s Graduate Development Programme is for Omani graduates, and OQ’s programme took 130 graduates in 2026; Oman Airports’ graduate programme asked for Omani nationality.
atlas-om.0053: Omanis made up 90.2% of government employment in 2025 and 47.1% of new government recruits held a bachelor’s degree or equivalent; the public sector is a graduate employer for Omanis, not for foreigners.
atlas-om.0054: Marketing specialists and sales representatives are already among the professions closed to new expatriate hires.
atlas-om.0055: IT is being localised step by step: systems analysts from 2025, programmers and computer engineers from 2026, web designers and operations analysts from 2027.
atlas-om.0056: University fairs cluster between January and April and programme postings come in autumn (Oman Airports on 1 October 2025); the pages read show no single national season.
atlas-om.0057: Employers surveyed in 2025 favoured bachelor’s holders, and the Oman Airports programme accepted a bachelor’s or a master’s; we found no posting that treats a master’s as an advantage. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0058: The Ministry of Higher Education requires an equivalency certificate for qualifications issued abroad, in addition to attestation by the embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Oman Observer, 2018); Oman has been party to the Apostille Convention since 30 January 2012, and the library asks for apostilled degrees with a sworn translation. Engineers, logistics and accounting professionals also need a sectoral skills-unit assessment before arrival.
atlas-om.0059: Fairs are run by individual universities (SQU, Sohar University, the Internship Fair’s four partners) and the 2025 employer survey names fields, not schools; we found no ranking of schools by employers. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0060: We found no apprenticeship or dual-study route into graduate jobs; the library finds no stand-alone internship status and describes only curricular internships for students enrolled at Omani universities. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0061: At the end of June 2026 Omanis held 392,962 government jobs and 441,737 private-sector jobs, and they were 90.2% of government employment in 2025; the public sector is a major graduate employer for Omanis.
atlas-om.0062: Every foreign hire needs the employer to obtain the Ministry of Labour clearance by showing Omanisation compliance (the library gives fees of OMR 201 to 301, doubled for non-compliant firms); more than 200 professions are closed to new expatriate visas, and the library finds that junior posts cannot be cleared for foreigners. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-om.0063: A CV guide for Oman says a professional headshot is customary, especially for senior roles, but optional.
atlas-om.0064: The same guide advises a concise one-to-two-page resume for private-sector roles, up to three pages for senior or academic ones, with longer CVs common in government.
atlas-om.0065: The pages read (KPMG’s selection steps, OQ and Oman Airports) mention an online application and no cover letter. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0066: None of the programme pages read asks for references with the application. This is our reading.
atlas-om.0067: Degrees and certificates need the Ministry of Higher Education’s equivalency certificate and, per the library, a double apostille with a sworn translation into English or Arabic.
atlas-om.0068: We found no page saying Omani employers ask for a salary expectation with the first application; the contract states the basic wage, bonuses and allowances. This is our reading for the application stage.
atlas-om.0069: Checks run through the state for a foreign hire: equivalency of the degree, a Ministry of Health medical within 30 days of arrival (blood tests and a tuberculosis test), and, for regulated professions, a pre-arrival qualification assessment. Prosecutors reported 1,200 forgery cases between 2010 and 2016.
atlas-om.0070: Applications run through portals (the Ministry of Labour’s job-seeker service, the Oman Jobs board) and employer pages; a 2016 Huddersfield thesis based on 496 questionnaires in banking, tourism and car retailing found no significant impact from wasta and nepotism on barriers to Omanisation, though it covers Omani employees, not foreign graduates.
atlas-om.0071: Every job needs an employer-sponsored permit, and the employer must meet its Omanisation quota.
atlas-om.0072: The employer must complete the clearance and visa before you arrive; the library says the visa-free 14-day entry cannot be converted to a work visa inside the country (ROP directive of 31 October 2023).
atlas-om.0073: English is standard for multinational firms and Arabic is often required for government and local companies (CV guide); the labour contract must be written in Arabic in two copies, and KPMG’s online assessments include English.
atlas-om.0074: KPMG Middle East’s graduate programmes run six steps: online application, a meeting with the talent-attraction team, online assessments (English, logical and numerical reasoning, accounting), an in-house assessment centre with interviews, a case study and a group activity, an offer, then an onboarding bootcamp.
atlas-om.0075: For the Omani-only programmes the first step is registration as a job seeker with the Ministry of Labour (Oman Airports); for a foreign hire, the library gives 7 to 10 working days officially and 2 to 4 working weeks in practice for the clearance and visa, then a medical within 30 days of arrival.
atlas-om.0076: We did not establish interview language, dress norms or assessment-centre practice beyond KPMG’s steps, nor the selection steps of PDO, OQ or Oman Airports.
atlas-om.0077: The labour contract must be written, in Arabic, in two copies and approved by the competent authority; a fixed term cannot exceed five years, and a contract with no term, an unwritten one, or one that runs on after expiry becomes indefinite.
atlas-om.0078: Probation must be in the contract and cannot exceed three months for monthly-paid workers (two months for others), only once with the same employer, with 7 days’ notice to end it. Notice for a legitimate termination is 30 days for monthly-paid workers and 15 days for others, and the worker gets up to ten paid hours a week to look for a new job.
atlas-om.0079: End-of-service gratuity under the labour law in force since 31 July 2023 is not less than one basic wage per year of service; for expatriates it applies until a savings system funded at 9% of basic wage by the employer replaces it, and we did not establish whether that has started. The employer, not the worker, pays the work-permit fees.
atlas-om.0080: We did not establish whether graduates negotiate, how long employers give to decide, or entry pay.
atlas-om.0081: Ministerial Decree 501/2024 amends Decree 235/2022 and adds professions closed to new expatriate hires in phases (marketing specialists, sales representatives and quality-control officers from 2 September 2024; systems analysts from 2025; programmers and computer engineers from 2026; web designers and operations analysts from 2027), on top of the older list; the Ministry announced in January 2026 that more than 200 professions are covered, and existing workers may stay until their permits expire.
atlas-om.0082: Banks are the clearest case: the central bank’s 2013 circular asks for Omanisation above 90% overall and 100% in clerical posts, so a foreign graduate has little room outside senior or specialist roles at foreign banks. This is our reading of the last point.
atlas-om.0083: Ask early who sponsors, whether the job title is on the closed list and whether the role counts toward Omanisation; the library finds that entry-level and junior posts cannot be cleared for foreigners, and that an employer may dismiss an expatriate to replace him or her with an Omani.
atlas-om.0084: Public services and boards: the Ministry of Labour (mol.gov.om) lets job seekers register, apply for private and government jobs and share their profile with employers; the Oman Jobs board (omanjobs.om) has jobseeker, employer, fresh-graduate or trainee and recruitment-consultant accounts.
atlas-om.0085: Employer pages: OQ’s graduate hiring programme (oq.com/en/careers/graduate-hiring-program, for young Omanis), KPMG Oman’s graduate development programme (kpmg.com/om) and PDO’s Graduate Development Programme (for Omani staff).
atlas-om.0086: University services and fairs: SQU’s Centre for Career Guidance and Career & Training Fair, Sohar University’s Career Training Fair and the Oman Internship Fair in January.
atlas-om.0087: Applying under a closed title: the library says the Ministry of Labour system automatically rejects requests for marketing specialist, sales representative or HR manager roles and, from 1 January 2026, computer programmer or computer engineer.
